label: sec:ns-approaches-intro
html: The classical Navier--Stokes regularity question sits inside a one-parameter family of well-posed q-deformed equations. The degeneration at q = 1 forms a research programme. We treat the classical limit as a phase transition and identify the critical exponent of enstrophy divergence. This structural prediction depends only on the Euler characteristic. We formulate a q-deformed Aubin--Lions compactness lemma and adapt the Beale--Kato--Majda blowup criterion. We track the geometry of vortex collision via the Levi degeneracy and explicit Townsend strain dynamics. Finally, we provide a self-similar Leray blowup profile constrained by \mathrm{SU}_q(2) representation theory.
